title: Claude Shannon and the Physical Realization of Logic (1937)
explainer: In 1937, MIT graduate student Claude Shannon wrote a master's thesis, 'A Symbolic Analysis of Relay and Switching Circuits,' showing that Boolean algebra's true/false values map directly onto open and closed electromechanical relay switches. That insight is the bridge between the abstract AND/OR/NOT symbols in a truth table and an actual physical circuit built from switching elements - the same bridge that later lets transistors stand in for relays. It's widely regarded as the theoretical starting point for digital circuit design as an engineering discipline.
